newsitem.title: GERMANY: German April s/a unemployment rises slightly.
newsitem.headline: German April s/a unemployment rises slightly.

text.p: German unemployment rose slightly to a seasonally adjusted 4.299 million in April, the Federal Labour Office said on Tuesday.
The unemployment rate, which is based on unadjusted data, fell to 11.3 percent, compared with 11.7 percent in March. The number of unemployed workers rose by 8,000 from March.
Unadjusted April unemployment -- the most politically sensitive figure in Germany -- fell to 4.347 million from 4.477 million in March, the Labour Office said.
Those figures confirmed numbers leaked by sources with access to official data on Monday.

In western Germany, the number of people out of work on a seasonally adjusted basis rose by 6,000 in April to 3.016 million. Eastern Germany added 2,000 to unemployment rolls, reaching a total 1.284 million.
Peter Hintze, the general secretary of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats, said: "We can achieve a turnaround in the jobs market. The new figures show that."
